blocks.prompt: 11. Sum the series to \(n\) terms \(2 + 5x + 8x^{2} + 11x^{3} + \cdots\) and deduce the sum to infinity if \(|x| < 1\).
blocks.explanation:
An A.G.P.: A.P. part \(2, 5, 8, 11, \ldots\) (\(d = 3\)), G.P. part \(1, x, x^2, \ldots\).
Two answers: \(S_n\) by multiply-by-\(x\)-and-subtract; then for \(|x| < 1\) let \(n \to \infty\) (powers of \(x\) die out).
Plan: \(T_n\), \(S_n\) and \(xS_n\), subtract, sum the G.P., divide by \(1 - x\); then the limit, and check with \(S_\infty\).
steps:
Given: \(2 + 5x + 8x^{2} + 11x^{3} + \cdots\); A.P. \(a = 2, d = 3\); G.P. \(b = 1, r = x\)
To find: \(S_n\), and \(S_\infty\) when \(|x| < 1\).
Method: Multiply-by-\(r\)-and-subtract (the method of 6.8.1): write \(S_n\), write \(rS_n\) one place to the right, subtract; the middle becomes a G.P. that we can sum. For \(S_\infty\): as \(n \to \infty\), \(x^n \to 0\) and \(nx^n \to 0\) when \(|x| < 1\).

The \(n\)th term
\[T_n = (3n - 1)x^{n-1}\]
Why: A.P. \(n\)th term \(2 + (n - 1)3 = 3n - 1\); G.P. \(n\)th term \(x^{n-1}\).

Write \(S_n\) and \(xS_n\)
\[S_n = 2 + 5x + 8x^{2} + \cdots + (3n - 1)x^{n-1}\]
\[xS_n = 2x + 5x^{2} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + (3n - 4)x^{n-1} + (3n - 1)x^{n}\]
Why: Multiply by \(x\) and shift; the second-last term \((3n - 4)x^{n-2}\) becomes \((3n - 4)x^{n-1}\).

Subtract
\[(1 - x)S_n = 2 + 3x + 3x^{2} + \cdots\]
\[\quad + 3x^{n-1} - (3n - 1)x^{n}\]
\[= 2 + 3(x + x^{2} + \cdots + x^{n-1})\]
\[\quad - (3n - 1)x^{n}\]
Why: Each pair leaves \(d = 3\) times the power, e.g. \((5 - 2)x = 3x\); the first term 2 stays (it does not fit \(3x^k\)).

Sum the G.P. and divide by \(1 - x\)
\[x + \cdots + x^{n-1} = \dfrac{x(1 - x^{n-1})}{1 - x}\]
\[S_n = \dfrac{2}{1 - x} + \dfrac{3x(1 - x^{n-1})}{(1 - x)^{2}}\]
\[\quad - \dfrac{(3n - 1)x^{n}}{1 - x}\]
Why: G.P.: first term \(x\), ratio \(x\), \(n - 1\) terms; then divide every term by \(1 - x\).

Check \(S_n\) with \(n = 1\) and \(n = 2\)
\[n = 1:\ \dfrac{2}{1 - x} - \dfrac{2x}{1 - x} = 2 \;\checkmark\]
\[n = 2:\ \dfrac{2 + 3x - 5x^{2}}{1 - x}\]
\[= \dfrac{(1 - x)(2 + 5x)}{1 - x} = 2 + 5x \;\checkmark\]
Why: For \(n = 1\) the middle term is 0 since \(1 - x^0 = 0\).

Deduce the sum to infinity
\[|x| < 1:\ x^{n-1} \to 0,\ (3n - 1)x^{n} \to 0\]
\[S_\infty = \dfrac{2}{1 - x} + \dfrac{3x}{(1 - x)^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2(1 - x) + 3x}{(1 - x)^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2 + x}{(1 - x)^{2}}\]
Why: When \(|x| < 1\) the powers of \(x\) shrink to 0 faster than \(n\) grows, so the last term vanishes; then combine over \((1 - x)^2\).

Check with the formula
\[S_\infty = \dfrac{ab}{1 - r} + \dfrac{dbr}{(1 - r)^{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{2}{1 - x} + \dfrac{3x}{(1 - x)^{2}} \;\checkmark\]
Why: With \(a = 2, d = 3, b = 1, r = x\) the 6.8.2 formula gives the same \(S_\infty\).
